What is the reward for one whose eyes shed tears with Your fear?” The reply was, “O Moosa (a.s)! I shall save his face from the heat of the Hellfire and prevent him from the hardship of the Hereafter!” The Prophet of Islam (a.s) said, “One whose eyes water with the fear of Allah, in return for every drop of his tears Allah will give him a palace in the Heaven. The palace will be decorated with pearls and precious stones.” Imam Jafar e Sadiq (a.s) said: If the sins create such a distance between the sinner and the Heaven that will be equivalent to the distance between the Firmament and the Taht as sara, the person will grieve and cry that the Heaven comes close to him as the eye is to the eye-lashes! The people who cry over their sins with Allahs fear in the world, will be happy with Allah’s Mercies on the Day of Judgement. Everything has a weight and measure. But a single drop of tear of compunction can cool the fire of many rivers of fire in the Hell. The face that carries the tears of remorse over the sins committed, Allah will make the Hellfire Haram on him. A people who have even one person who grieves and mourns, Allah will have His Mercy on the entire community! Imam Mohammed Baqir (a.s) said, “The tears that flow with Allah’s fear on the cheeks in the darkness of night, are more pleasing to Allah than anything else.” Imam Jafar e Sadiq (a.s) has said, “On the Day of Judgement all the eyes will be crying excepting of three persons. One of them who closed his eyes to the things that have been pronounced as Haram by Allah. Another is the person whose eyes remained open in obedience to Allah. The third person is that whose eyes shed tears with fear of Allah in the nights.” Ishaq bin Ammar narrates that he told to Imam Jafar e Sadiq (a.s): O Imam (a.s)! I want to cry but tears don’t come out! Many a time I try to remember the dead of my kith and kin thinking that it might give vent to my tears. Is it legitimate to do this? The Imam (a.s) said, “It is legitimate! But when you start crying get busy remembering Allah!” The Imam (a.s) said at another occasion, “If you are unable to cry, put your thoughts on it! Even if you get a tear as small as a fly, it will be good for you!” Imam Jafar e Sadiq (a.s) said once, “When you have any fear or you have a wish to make, then first praise Allah. Then call for peace on the Prophet (a.s) and his Ahl e Bayt (a.s). Then submit to Allah for His 251Mercies! Man will be closest to Allah when he has his head in the prostration of prayer and is crying for His Help.” The Prophet of Islam (a.s) has said: O Abu Dharr! Seven persons will be such that Allah will give them place in His Firmament on the Day of Judgement. They will be: (1) The Just Imam (Imam e Adil) (2) The truthful youth. (3) The person who does charity hidden from others. (4) One who remembers Allah in seclusion. (5) One who makes friends with momins to please Allah. (6) One who emerges from the Mosque thinking that he would return to it again. (7) One whom a beautiful woman tries to entice, but he says with Allah’s Fear that he is afraid and fearful. O Abu Dharr! Allah said, ‘I shall not have two fears with my creatures at the same time. One who fears me in the World, I shall have him fearless in the Hereafter. Better yet, how much does one need if he requires it to survive? I found myself wondering about that this morning as I stepped out of my room. It felt brighter than normal, and by pure instinct I found myself squinting my eyes as I headed to the designated mens bathroom. An extra switch that I dont normally turn on had been activated by the CNA in charge this morning. Not a problem, I thought to myself. Not only can I tolerate having some more light, I welcomed it. Yesterday was the birthday of a dear housemate and friend, and we found different ways to celebrate, including seeing Twisters at the Cinemark Palace 20 (a very good movie that nearly lives up to the 1996 classic which served as its inspiration) and a surprise dinner at the Olive Garden near my old house--inspired by this housemates love of Italian food--as this is, apparently, the closest Olive Garden to where I live now. Its unfortunate that the weekend house manager had to drive such a long way, but I am glad she did. I found myself being initially attracted by the Shrimp Fritto Misto, and after going over several other possibilities--including a suggestion of getting Fettucini Alfredo--I came back to my original choice. I am glad I did, as I got more or less the same number of calories for several dollars less and came in well under my $21 limit. (Not sure why they didnt just make it an even $20, but an extra dollar is nothing to complain about.) The birthday girl had the Lasagna Classico and a complementary Chocolate Lasagna for dessert. I felt bad when we ended up having to go without her having eaten a single bite of the latter, as she wanted to share it with her housemates. The cake came on a platter with multiple spoons, yet somehow we were not provided with extra dessert plates. Earlier that day, I listened to STR8Fightahs In My Eyez and kept replaying one lyric in my mind, where he references his favorite fighter, Rubin Hurricane Carter. I was inspired to take that song, slow it down, and down-sample it to 8 kHz VOX ADPCM. The VOX format is compatible with OKI6295, a legendary sound IC that was used in hundreds of arcade games, and possibly well over a thousand. (Thats just counting unique games, not including bootlegs and updates of already existing titles.) Without getting too technical, ADPCM compression can result in a gritty, grimy sound suitable for hip-hop, especially at lower sample rates. 8 kHz is a good balance of small file sizes and fidelity. The OKI6295 could accept samples up to 256KB; at 8 kHz that comes out to just over a minute of audio. In my case, I would have needed to break the samples up and implement a bank-switching system to play them one after the other, or keep the song at its original tempo (or speed it up ever so slightly) to keep it within the 256KB limit. Not a problem, as the point of this experiment was to see what ADPCM compression would do to the song when combined with slowing down the pitch and tempo. I feel like it sounds good this way, good enough so that I was compelled to take a couple of my old T-shirts that I brought with me and write R.I.P. RUBIN HURRICANE CARTER on the back of them. (I had written on another shirt in the past, one that reads THREE DAYS UNTIL MARIO STEALS YOUR LIVER, referencing a meme from several years ago that most people have already forgotten about.) I opted to customize my hat in a similar way, writing R.I.P. JACQUI and R.I.P. RICHARD in memory of my deceased parents. On the brim I initially wrote R.I.P. RUBIN CARTER, squeezing in the word HURRICANE when I saw there was enough space to do so. I have found myself inspired by the story of Carter, a courageous middleweight best known for knocking out the renowned Emile Griffith in one round, and for his title shot against Joey Giardello (a loss over 15 rounds, which is nothing to be ashamed of as he had only 24 pro bouts going in [including the TKO of Griffith], whereas the champion was a veteran of 128 pro fights). He was wrongly convicted and imprisoned for murder, serving almost 20 years in Rahway State Prison before being released following a habeas corpus petition; to this day, it is a powerful story, one reflecting the racial injustice of the times, and inspired him to become an advocate for others in a similar situation, culminating in his becoming executive director of what is today known as Innocence Canada(but at the time was known as the Association in Defence of the Wrongly Convicted). He was just as courageous outside the ring as he was in the squared circle. In 1996, three years into an eventual twelve as AIDWYCs executive director, he was arrested after being mistakenly identified by Toronto police as a thirty-something suspect believed to have sold drugs to an undercover officer. (He was 59 at the time and I cant help but be reminded of the saying about how black dont crack.) Of course, when the police realized their error, he was released. A damning reflection on the state of race relations in the 1990s; one cannot help but wonder just how far society as a whole had come in the several decades since Carters boxing career was ended due to the original false accusations. Having had a chance to look through a box containing several items from my Moms old office at her former place of employment, my eyes are drawn to a crystal plaque gifted to her by her friends at PROPEL (People Reaching Out to Provide Education and Leadership), which she co-founded back in 2002, and more specifically the following words: For your Selfless Devotion to our Mission - For your Commitment and Dedication - For your Integrity and Purity of Spirit - We at PROPEL, will Forever be Grateful - May God Bless You Always. I cant help but smile; in a few words, whoever wrote that had managed to capture all of the qualities that made her who she was, and which inspire me to do my best in my current endeavors. To the right of that plaque is a portrait of me following my graduation from Florida Atlantic University in 2014, covered in various sashes and ribbons, wearing a medal and a cap with a tassel. I am drawn to the smile on my face. The future seemed so promising, until it wasnt. Maybe there is still time to make a difference. Perhaps I didnt throw my potential away after all. The old, water-damaged photograph of me with the Mathematics certificate still hangs on my wall, held up by two repurposed pieces of tape. A coincidentally tombstone-shaped piece of cardboard can now be found in close proximity with R.I.P. RUBIN HURRICANE CARTER on it, held up by a yellow pushpin that was being redundantly used to secure a small U.S. flag upon the wall. Inspiration in many forms. Heres a detailed look at what Ive learned, which I hope can provide some guidance for those still finding their way.  #### 1. Doing More For A Man Does Not Mean Hell Value You More It’s a common misconception that going out of your way to do things for a man will make him value you more. In reality, it often results in him valuing himself more, while you may find yourself feeling unappreciated. Focus on what truly matters to you and maintain those standards to ensure you’re respected and valued.  #### 2. Invest In Yourself Prioritize your own growth and happiness. When a man sees that you have a fulfilling life and are continuously working on improving yourself, he will naturally see you as more valuable. Self-investment is the best investment you’ll ever make.  #### 3. Be A Mirror For His Aspirations Men often want to feel like the incredible people they aspire to be through your eyes. This doesn’t mean abandoning your opinions or values; it means being supportive and showing appreciation. Be a strong, opinionated woman, but also show them that you recognize their worth.  #### 4. Strike A Balance: Hard to Get, Easy to Be With Men are often drawn to women who are hard to get yet easy to be with. Create a fun, independent life for yourself that makes you less available, but when you are present, be playful, joyous, and positive. Never bottle up your needs; communicate upfront to avoid any future resentment.  #### 5. Confidence Is Key Knowing your worth is essential. Remember the golden rule: if he wants to, he will; if he doesn’t, he won’t. If a man is unsure about you, that’s a clear sign you should be unsure too. Follow his lead and meet him at his level of commitment.  #### 6. Respect The Need For Space Even in the healthiest of relationships, space is crucial. When he needs some distance, don’t close the gap; instead, grant him the space he desires. Relationships flourish when both individuals can maintain their personal power and independence.  #### 7. Believe People When They Show You Who They Are Accept people for who they genuinely are. If you spend your time trying to change them, it implies you don’t truly love or respect their authentic selves. Understanding and acceptance are the cornerstones of any stable relationship.  #### 8. Initiate The Connection Never just let the man pick you; you must also make a conscious choice. Invite the man into your world—be an active participant in the relationship and remember that your choice matters just as much.  #### 9. Embrace Shared Values Over Looks While physical attraction is important, shared values should be the bedrock of any long-standing relationship. Focus on finding someone whose beliefs and values align with yours for a deeper, more meaningful connection.  #### 10. Emotional Readiness Before Physical Intimacy Sleeping with a man can often result in a deeper emotional attachment. Make sure you’re emotionally ready before taking that step. True emotional connection and commitment are what keep relationships strong, not just physical attraction.  ### Additional Insights  #### Protect Your Energy Be cautious of low vibrational men who don’t meet your needs. A man who is not right for you will find your normal efforts overwhelming and may start to devalue you. Rather than lowering yourself to meet his standards, look for someone who steps up to meet yours. A man who cant see your worth is not worth your time.  #### Silent Communication Of Boundaries Sometimes, the strongest statements are made without uttering a word. Radiate high-value energy by mastering the art of silent communication. Establish your boundaries through your actions and choices instead of constant verbal reminders.  #### Decenter Men, Center Yourself Your life should not revolve around your partner. Focus on your growth, your happiness, and your goals. The right man will fit into your life seamlessly without demanding to be the center of attention.  #### Embrace Positive Vibes Radiate positive energy and high self-esteem. When you vibrate on this level, the right kind of people—including potential partners—will be naturally drawn to you.  ### Conclusion Reflecting on my 20s, these lessons have been instrumental in helping me navigate relationships with more clarity and confidence. Remember, your time and love are invaluable. Focus on investing in yourself and finding someone who truly deserves the incredible person you are. Here’s to making smarter choices and building fulfilling relationships.
